title: CREST syndrome (limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis)
diseaseDescription: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (CREST: calcinosis, Raynaud's phenomenon, oesophageal dysmotility, sclerodactyly, telangiectasia). This bounded map covers anticentromere autoimmunity, endothelial/vascular injury with a pulmonary arterial hypertension branch, fibroblast activation and calcinosis associations. Many mechanistic findings come from mixed SSc cohorts, cell culture or animal models and are not lcSSc-specific. Diffuse-cutaneous-specific mechanisms, scleroderma renal crisis, morphea, overlap syndromes and therapies are out of scope.
releaseNote: Initial bounded CREST/lcSSc candidate from 29 primary reports (Europe PMC abstracts only). Associations, in-vitro mechanisms and animal-model findings remain distinct; several null/qualifying results are retained (ACA vs PAH within CREST, IL-6 predominance in dcSSc, inverse ACA-ILD association; further null results that lack a supported edge are retained in the workspace packet). Source checks were performed by agents, not humans. Independent domain review is pending; all scores are unassessed; no therapies are curated.

entities.label: Anticentromere antibodies
entities.description: Autoantibodies to centromere proteins (chiefly CENP-B), the serological marker most strongly linked to limited cutaneous SSc / CREST.

entities.label: HLA class II risk alleles
entities.description: HLA-DRB1/DQA1/DQB1/DPB1 alleles and haplotypes associated with SSc and its autoantibody subsets.

entities.label: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells
entities.description: Type I interferon-producing dendritic cells; studied in SSc blood and skin.

entities.label: CXCL4 (platelet factor 4)
entities.description: Chemokine reported as the predominant protein secreted by SSc plasmacytoid dendritic cells.

entities.label: Type I interferon signature
entities.description: Type I interferon production or interferon-inducible gene/chemokine activity.

entities.label: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
entities.description: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (including 'intrinsic' PH without major lung fibrosis) in SSc.

entities.label: Telangiectasia
entities.description: Cutaneous telangiectasiae, a CREST feature.

entities.label: Interstitial lung disease
entities.description: SSc-associated interstitial lung disease / pulmonary fibrosis.

entities.label: Calcinosis cutis
entities.description: Subcutaneous/cutaneous calcium deposits, a CREST feature.

entities.label: Clinically meaningful progression in lcSSc
entities.description: Time to clinical worsening on the MINIMISE combined morbi-mortality endpoint in limited cutaneous SSc.

entities.label: Digital ulcers
entities.description: Ischaemic ulceration of the digits in systemic sclerosis.

entities.label: Digital ischaemia
entities.description: Clinical digital ischaemic manifestations in SSc (digital ulcers, pitting scars, gangrene), as defined by the reporting cohort.

entities.label: Acro-osteolysis
entities.description: Resorption of the distal phalangeal tufts on hand imaging in SSc.

entities.label: Ulnar artery occlusion
entities.description: Ultrasound-detected occlusion of the ulnar artery, a macrovascular manifestation of SSc vasculopathy.

entities.label: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP-4)
entities.description: Osteogenic/pro-calcifying TGF-beta superfamily ligand.

entities.label: TGF-beta
entities.description: Transforming growth factor-beta; here the autocrine TGF-beta loop in cultured SSc dermal fibroblasts.

entities.label: IL-6
entities.description: Interleukin-6, including trans-signalling via soluble IL-6 receptor.

entities.label: Dermal fibroblasts
entities.description: Dermal fibroblasts explanted from SSc or healthy skin and studied in culture.

entities.label: Myofibroblasts
entities.description: Alpha-SMA-expressing contractile fibroblasts.

entities.label: Collagen / extracellular-matrix deposition
entities.description: Type I collagen gene/protein expression and ECM production.

entities.label: Skin fibrosis
entities.description: Clinically measured skin thickening (e.g. modified Rodnan skin score).

entities.label: Endothelial cells
entities.description: Vascular endothelial cells; here HUVECs in vitro.

entities.label: Oesophageal dysmotility
entities.description: Oesophageal hypomotility measured by transit scintigraphy or high-resolution manometry.

entities.label: Integrin alpha-v beta-3
entities.description: Integrin that binds latency-associated peptide and activates latent TGF-beta1; upregulated on SSc fibroblasts.

entities.label: Limited cutaneous SSc (subset)
entities.description: The limited cutaneous SSc clinical subset as a cohort grouping; used only to anchor subset-level prevalence findings.

entities.label: Anti-endothelial cell antibodies
entities.description: Circulating antibodies binding endothelial cells; studied here mainly in the UCD-200 chicken model of scleroderma.

entities.label: Endothelial injury / apoptosis
entities.description: Endothelial cell damage or apoptosis, and circulating markers of vascular injury, in SSc and its models.

entities.label: Endothelin-1
entities.description: Endothelium-derived vasoconstrictor peptide with profibrotic effects on fibroblasts.

entities.label: Centromere proteins (CENP-A/B/C)
entities.description: Kinetochore/centromere proteins; CENP-B is the major autoantigen recognized by anticentromere antibodies.

claims.text: Among patients with the CREST variant of SSc, ACA-positive patients more often had calcinosis than ACA-negative CREST patients; ACA itself was found in about half of CREST patients versus 3% of diffuse disease.
limitations: Observational, single-centre, older classification (CREST variant vs diffuse) and pre-modern ACA assays
Calcinosis association is not causal evidence

claims.text: Within CREST-variant SSc, ACA positivity was associated with a higher frequency of digital telangiectasiae.
limitations: Observational, single-centre, 1984 cohort
Telangiectasia was common in both groups (75% in ACA-negative)

claims.text: Within CREST-variant SSc, PAH frequency did not differ between ACA-positive and ACA-negative patients, so ACA did not discriminate PAH risk inside the limited subset in this cohort.
limitations: Comparison is within CREST patients only, not ACA+ vs all SSc
Small numbers and 1984-era PAH ascertainment (no routine right-heart catheterisation screening)

claims.text: In ACA-positive lcSSc patients, 'intrinsic' pulmonary hypertension (without major lung fibrosis) occurred in 19%, higher than previously reported, though the authors note possible referral bias.
limitations: Retrospective record review at a referral centre; authors flag referral bias
No ACA-negative or healthy comparator for PH frequency; single-autoantibody patients only

claims.text: Inverse association: ACA-positive lcSSc patients had the lowest incidence of clinically significant pulmonary fibrosis (8.5%) among antibody/skin subsets in a 1,325-patient SSc cohort.
limitations: The association is inverse (lower ILD incidence with ACA); the symmetric edge does not imply ACA promotes ILD
Single-centre tertiary cohort; observational

claims.text: In a multi-ethnic US case-control study, the ACA-positive subset was best explained by HLA-DQB1*0501 and DQB1 alleles lacking leucine at position 26 (DQB1 26 epi).
limitations: Genetic association; SSc cohort, ACA subset analysis rather than lcSSc-defined cases
ACA-allele association reported for white and Hispanic subjects; not replicated in all ancestries (e.g. a Japanese study did not confirm the position-26 association, PMID 8546531, not included)

claims.text: Proteome-wide analysis of plasmacytoid dendritic cells isolated from SSc patients identified CXCL4 as their predominant secreted protein, in circulation and skin.
limitations: SSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific
Platelets are also a major CXCL4 source; abstract does not quantify pDC contribution to plasma levels

claims.text: Plasma CXCL4 levels were markedly elevated in SSc and correlated with skin and lung fibrosis and with pulmonary arterial hypertension.
limitations: Correlational; SSc cohort, not lcSSc-specific
Abstract does not report effect sizes for the PAH correlation

claims.text: pDCs infiltrate the skin of SSc patients and are chronically activated, secreting IFN-alpha (and CXCL4).
limitations: SSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific
Mouse pDC-depletion data in the same report are not encoded here

claims.text: In a lcSSc cohort, a high serum type I IFN chemokine score predicted shorter time to clinical worsening (MINIMISE composite), independently of clinical variables.
limitations: Retrospective; IFN score is a surrogate from six interferon-inducible chemokines, not direct IFN measurement
Prognostic association, not causal

claims.text: In a large retrospective multicentre SSc cohort, digital ulcers were among the strongest independent correlates of calcinosis in multivariable analysis.
limitations: SSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific
Retrospective cross-sectional association; temporal order of ulcers and calcinosis not established
Calcinosis ascertainment varied across centres

claims.text: Anticentromere antibodies were more frequent in SSc patients with calcinosis than without, whereas anti-Scl-70, anti-RNA polymerase III and U1-RNP were less common.
limitations: Univariate comparison; ACA was not among the strongest independent associations reported in multivariable analysis
SSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific, so ACA may partly mark the limited subset/longer disease duration
Association only; no mechanistic link between ACA and mineralisation

claims.text: In an international SSc cohort, digital ischaemia was independently associated with calcinosis (alongside disease duration), consistent with a vascular/ischaemic hypothesis for SSc calcinosis.
limitations: SSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific
Cross-sectional association; does not show ischaemia causes calcinosis
Tissue hypoxia not directly measured

claims.text: Acro-osteolysis was independently associated with calcinosis in a multicentre SSc cohort; the same study found lower bone-density T-scores in patients with calcinosis.
limitations: SSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific
Cross-sectional association; shared ischaemic or bone-remodelling drivers are possible confounders
Bone densitometry available in only 68 patients

claims.text: In EUSTAR, SSc patients with calcinosis at baseline more often had telangiectasia, digital ischaemia and late capillaroscopy patterns, linking calcinosis to the CREST microvascular phenotype.
limitations: SSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific; per the raw abstract, dcSSc also predicted 10-year incident calcinosis (OR 1.51), arguing against lcSSc specificity

Baseline univariate comparison; per the raw abstract telangiectasia (OR 1.92) and digital ulcers (OR 2.60-2.92) also predicted incident calcinosis, but that sentence is lost by the repo plainText normaliser (see notes) so is not quoted
Registry ascertainment of calcinosis; association only

claims.text: On ultrasound, ulnar artery occlusion was strongly associated with radiograph-identified hand calcinosis (per-hand OR 8.08), supporting a macrovascular/ischaemic link to SSc calcinosis.
limitations: Small sample with very wide confidence intervals
Mixed dcSSc/lcSSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific
Per the raw abstract, finger pulp blood flow and the composite perfusion score were not significantly associated (partial null), and UAO remained associated in hands without digital ulcers (OR 33.00)
Cross-sectional

claims.text: In female SSc patients, serum BMP-4 was higher in those with calcinosis; fetuin-A was proposed as a possible prognostic marker and lower serum calcification propensity (T50) correlated with clinical manifestation burden.
limitations: Small single-centre sample, women only
SSc subsets not specified in abstract; not lcSSc-specific
Fetuin-A finding stated only as potential; cross-sectional

claims.text: In a Japanese SSc cohort with hand radiographs, calcinosis was more prevalent in ACA-positive patients, whereas acro-osteolysis was less common with ACA.
limitations: SSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific
Cross-sectional; effect size not given in abstract
Single centre; calcinosis assessed on hand radiographs only

claims.text: In cultured dermal fibroblasts, TGF-beta receptor overexpression increased alpha2(I) collagen promoter activity in a manner dependent on autocrine TGF-beta, and SSc fibroblasts expressed about 2-fold more TGF-beta receptors, which correlated with collagen mRNA.
limitations: SSc fibroblasts not stratified by cutaneous subset; not lcSSc-specific
Promoter-reporter transfection assays; in vitro only
1998 study; small number of cell strains (abstract does not specify)

claims.text: Overexpressing integrin alpha-v beta-3 in normal fibroblasts raised collagen promoter activity, and this effect depended on TGF-beta. This points to alpha-v beta-3 activating latent TGF-beta as part of the autocrine loop seen in SSc fibroblasts.
limitations: SSc subset not stated in abstract; not lcSSc-specific
Overexpression and antibody blockade in culture; in vivo causality not tested

claims.text: Blocking alpha-v beta-3 (which keeps autocrine TGF-beta signalling going) reversed type I procollagen overexpression and the myofibroblastic phenotype of SSc fibroblasts. This suggests that their myofibroblast-like state is maintained through this TGF-beta loop.
limitations: SSc subset not stated in abstract; not lcSSc-specific
Myofibroblast phenotype assessed in culture, not quantified in lcSSc skin

claims.text: In healthy dermal fibroblasts, IL-6 trans-signalling induced collagen I through STAT3. The effect was indirect: it ran through stronger TGF-beta/Smad3 signalling driven by induction of Gremlin-1.
limitations: Healthy-donor fibroblasts, not SSc or lcSSc cells
In vitro only; Europe PMC lists 'Clinical Trial' pub type, but the abstract describes in vitro experiments

claims.text: Serum IL-6 was often raised in SSc, mainly in diffuse cutaneous disease with thrombocytosis and raised acute-phase markers. In early dcSSc, high IL-6 was linked to more severe skin involvement at 3 years.
limitations: Elevation is concentrated in dcSSc; the abstract does not show it in lcSSc, which limits transfer to CREST
Observational association with skin outcome in early dcSSc only
Small control group

claims.text: Serum IL-6 positively correlated with modified Rodnan total skin thickness score in SSc; IL-6 was higher in diffuse than in limited cutaneous SSc.
limitations: SSc cohort; IL-6 elevation predominates in dcSSc, so relevance to lcSSc skin disease is limited
Cross-sectional serum correlation; cannot establish direction or causation

claims.text: CXCL4, or SSc-derived plasma, inhibited proliferation, migration and tube formation of HUVECs, and a CXCL4-neutralising antibody reversed this. CXCL4 downregulated Fli-1 via c-Abl. Plasma CXCL4 was higher in SSc and VEDOSS patients than in controls.
limitations: HUVECs are not dermal microvascular endothelium
SSc cohort not stratified by lcSSc in the abstract; not lcSSc-specific
Effect on dermal fibroblasts not assessed in this study

claims.text: Oesophageal dysmotility on transit scintigraphy was common in lcSSc (58.5% abnormal), though less frequent than in dcSSc (95.4%). Motility worsened over time in 58.8% of lcSSc patients versus 96% of dcSSc patients.
limitations: Retrospective; only patients with at least 2 scintigraphy studies (selection bias toward symptomatic patients)
Scintigraphy measures transit, not smooth-muscle atrophy or fibrosis histology
Small dcSSc comparator group

claims.text: In UCD-200/206 chicken skin, endothelial cells are the first cells to undergo apoptosis, a process the authors suggest is induced by anti-endothelial cell antibodies.
limitations: Animal model (UCD-200/206 chickens), not human lcSSc
AECA induction is inferred ('seems to be induced'), not directly tested in this study
SSc overall; not lcSSc-specific

claims.text: Transfer of AECA-positive UCD-200 sera into healthy chicken embryos/CAMs increased microvascular endothelial cell apoptosis versus controls, supporting a pathogenic role for AECA in vivo.
limitations: Avian model; not human lcSSc
Whole-serum transfer, so effect not proven to be specific to AECA
Effect seen 'in most groups', not all

claims.text: Endothelin had dose-dependent mitogenic and collagen synthesis-enhancing effects on cultured fibroblasts, linking the vasoconstrictor to a profibrotic action.
limitations: Fibroblast origin (dermal vs other, patient vs control) not stated in abstract
In vitro exogenous peptide; not lcSSc-specific
Small 1991 study

claims.text: In lcSSc, serum ET-1 was raised only in patients with hypertensive lung or renal disease compared with lcSSc patients with only fibrotic dermal/lung disease, unlike dcSSc where ET-1 was elevated irrespective of organ involvement.
limitations: lcSSc comparison group combines pulmonary hypertension with hypertensive renal disease; PAH-specific effect not separable in abstract
Cross-sectional; lcSSc sample size not given in abstract
PHT definition (echo vs catheter) not stated

claims.text: ET-1 added to normal lung fibroblasts induced contractile/myofibroblast proteins including alpha-SMA, via ETA and a Rac/PI3K/Akt-dependent pathway, and enhanced matrix contraction.
limitations: Lung fibroblasts, not dermal; SSc fibroblasts from patients with pulmonary fibrosis (dcSSc-weighted), not lcSSc-specific
In vitro only

claims.text: In an EUSTAR cohort of SSc patients with newly diagnosed digital ulcers (61% limited cutaneous), PAH and multiple ulcers at diagnosis were associated with presence of digital ulcers at follow-up.
limitations: SSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific (61% lcSSc)
Observational; association only (OR 4.34 for PAH)
Cohort restricted to patients who already had DU
Industry-supported registry analysis

claims.text: Higher telangiectasia scores were associated with higher RVSP and with greater adjusted odds of catheter-confirmed PAH, suggesting telangiectases mark more widespread microvascular disease.
limitations: SSc cohort; not lcSSc-specific (adjusted for subtype)
Cross-sectional single centre; wide CI (1.78-85.9)

claims.text: Limited SSc patients with PAH showed raised circulating markers of vascular injury (VCAM-1, VEGF, von Willebrand factor) along with inflammatory cytokines compared with lSSc without PAH.
limitations: Small cross-sectional sample; cytokines measured in a subset
Circulating markers are indirect proxies of endothelial injury

claims.text: Sera from at least 96% of patients with anticentromere antibodies recognized cloned CENP-B, which carries multiple independent autoantibody epitopes.
limitations: Antigen recognition (binding) is encoded as an association; the predicate set has no antigen-target relation
Does not show that ACA are pathogenic
Patient subset composition not stated in abstract
